Question: Ten points are selected on the positive \(x\)-axis, \(\mathrm{X}^+,\) and five points are selected on the positive \(y\)-axis, \(\mathrm{Y}^+.\) The fifty segments connecting the ten selected points on \(\mathrm{X}^+\) to the five selected points on \(\mathrm{Y}^+\) are drawn. What is the maximum possible number of points of intersection of these fifty segments that could lie in the interior of the first quadrant?
Solution:
First count pairs of segments that cross. We must then show that their crossings can all occur at different points.

Choose two selected points \(X_1,X_2\) on the positive \(x\)-axis, in increasing order of distance from the origin, and similarly choose \(Y_1,Y_2\) on the positive \(y\)-axis. These four points form the convex quadrilateral \(X_1X_2Y_2Y_1\). Its diagonals \(X_1Y_2\) and \(X_2Y_1\) cross in the first quadrant. The other pairing, \(X_1Y_1\) and \(X_2Y_2\), consists of disjoint sides.

Segments sharing an endpoint cannot meet again in their interiors. Consequently, every crossing pair uses two distinct points from each axis, and each such selection gives exactly one crossing pair. There are therefore
\[
\binom{10}{2}\binom{5}{2}
=\frac{10\cdot9}{2}\cdot\frac{5\cdot4}{2}
=450
\]
crossing pairs. Several pairs might cross at the same point, so \(450\) is an upper bound on the number of distinct intersection points.

To attain it, fix five distinct positive \(y\)-axis points and select the \(x\)-axis points one at a time. Whenever a new point is selected, avoid drawing a new segment through any existing interior intersection. This excludes only finitely many positions: each existing intersection and each selected \(y\)-axis point determine a line, which meets the \(x\)-axis in at most one position. There are still positive positions available, even beyond all previously selected points.

New segments share their new \(x\)-axis endpoint, so they cannot meet one another inside the quadrant. If a new segment passed through a crossing of two older segments, that position was excluded. Thus this construction prevents every interior meeting of three or more segments. All \(450\) crossing pairs then give distinct points.

The maximum is \(\boxed{450}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
